blocks.raw: # Classify Data as PSI and PII
blocks.text: Classify Data as PSI and PII

blocks.raw: This document explains what PSI and PII mean, why both are required, how Capillary uses them to meet access control and data protection requirements, and how to classify data as PSI and PII.
blocks.text: This document explains what PSI and PII mean, why both are required, how Capillary uses them to meet access control and data protection requirements, and how to classify data as PSI and PII.

blocks.raw: # **What is PII (Personally Identifiable Information)**
blocks.text: What is PII (Personally Identifiable Information)

blocks.raw: PII refers to data that can directly or indirectly identify an individual. This data is subject to privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA.
blocks.text: PII refers to data that can directly or indirectly identify an individual. This data is subject to privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA.

blocks.raw: ## **Typical examples**
blocks.text: Typical examples

blocks.raw:
* Name
* Mobile number
* Email address
* External customer ID
* Any identifier that uniquely links data to a person
blocks.text: NameMobile numberEmail addressExternal customer IDAny identifier that uniquely links data to a person

blocks.raw: # **What is PSI (Potentially Sensitive Information)**
blocks.text: What is PSI (Potentially Sensitive Information)

blocks.raw: PSI refers to data that is sensitive in nature and must be protected from unauthorised access. This data may not always be legally classified as PII, but exposure can still create privacy or security risks.
blocks.text: PSI refers to data that is sensitive in nature and must be protected from unauthorised access. This data may not always be legally classified as PII, but exposure can still create privacy or security risks.

blocks.raw: ## **Typical examples**
blocks.text: Typical examples

blocks.raw:
* Health-related attributes (for example, blood group, smoking habit)
* Lifestyle or behavioural attributes
* Financial or demographic attributes that require restricted visibility
blocks.text: Health-related attributes (for example, blood group, smoking habit)Lifestyle or behavioural attributesFinancial or demographic attributes that require restricted visibility

blocks.raw: Capillary uses **PSI** to enforce access control and data masking, and **PII** to support data deletion and regulatory compliance.
blocks.text: Capillary uses PSI to enforce access control and data masking, and PII to support data deletion and regulatory compliance.

blocks.raw: The table below shows how different data types are treated by default and where configuration is allowed.
blocks.text: The table below shows how different data types are treated by default and where configuration is allowed.

blocks.raw:
| Field type                   | PII (Deletion & compliance)            | PSI (Masking & access control)     |
| :--------------------------- | :------------------------------------- | :--------------------------------- |
| First name                   | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| Last name                    | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| Mobile number                | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| Email address                | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| External ID                  | Always PII                             | Never PSI (always visible)         |
| V2 profile identifiers       | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| Communication channels       | Always PII                             | Always PSI                         |
| Payment attributes           | Configurable                           | Never PSI (always visible)         |
| Extended fields              | Customer-level only (configurable)     | Customer-level only (configurable) |
| Custom fields                | Customer-and card-level (configurable) | Customer-level only (configurable) |
| Behavioural event attributes | Not treated as PII                     | Configurable                       |

target.note: GFM table; watch for an empty `| |` header row

blocks.raw: ## Notes and clarifications
blocks.text: Notes and clarifications

blocks.raw:
* Always PII means the field is automatically included in deletion and compliance workflows.

* Always PSI means the field is masked unless the user or API client has PSI access.

* Configurable means you explicitly decide whether the field should be treated as PSI or PII.

* External ID is never masked to ensure system traceability and integration stability.

* Behavioural event attributes can be masked (PSI) but are not considered PII by default.

blocks.raw: ## Note: PSI and PII marking in connected organisations
blocks.text: Note: PSI and PII marking in connected organisations

blocks.raw: In a **Connected Organisation** setup, PSI and PII behaviour depends on where the field is defined.
blocks.text: In a Connected Organisation setup, PSI and PII behaviour depends on where the field is defined.

blocks.raw: **Extended fields**
blocks.text: Extended fields

blocks.raw:
* Extended fields defined at the **parent organisation** are **inherited by all child organisations**.
* PSI or PII marking applied at the parent level applies automatically across all connected child organisations.
* Child organisations cannot override PSI or PII settings for parent-level extended fields.
blocks.text: Extended fields defined at the parent organisation are inherited by all child organisations.PSI or PII marking applied at the parent level applies automatically across all connected child organisations.Child organisations cannot override PSI or PII settings for parent-level extended fields.

blocks.raw: **Custom fields**
blocks.text: Custom fields

blocks.raw:
* Custom fields follow **organisation-specific ownership**.
* PSI and PII marking applies **only within the organisation where the custom field is created**.
blocks.text: Custom fields follow organisation-specific ownership.PSI and PII marking applies only within the organisation where the custom field is created.

blocks.raw: **Behaviour**:
blocks.text: Behaviour:

blocks.raw:
* **Parent-level custom fields**
  * PSI/PII marking applies only at the parent organisation.
  * Child organisations cannot modify or override these settings.

* **Child-level custom fields**
  * PSI/PII marking applies only within that specific child organisation.
  * Other child organisations and the parent organisation are not affected.
blocks.text: Parent-level custom fieldsPSI/PII marking applies only at the parent organisation.Child organisations cannot modify or override these settings.Child-level custom fieldsPSI/PII marking applies only within that specific child organisation.Other child organisations and the parent organisation are not affected.

blocks.raw: # Classifying custom & extended fields as PII/PSI
blocks.text: Classifying custom & extended fields as PII/PSI

blocks.raw: To classify a custom field or extended field as PSI/PII, perform the following:
blocks.text: To classify a custom field or extended field as PSI/PII, perform the following:

blocks.raw:
1. Navigate to Organisation settings > Data model>Custom fields/Extended fields.
2. Edit the custom field or extended field.
3. Select the **Is this pii data ?** or **Is this psi data ?** checkbox as required.

   <Image align="center" border={true} src="https://files.readme.io/c63da859468046b337bdff66d21f4760a2f5b7d552fbcd1c0329c82076b9d6da-image1.png" className="border" />
4. Click **Submit**.
blocks.text: Navigate to Organisation settings > Data model>Custom fields/Extended fields.Edit the custom field or extended field.Select the Is this pii data ? or Is this psi data ? checkbox as required.Click Submit.

blocks.raw: The selected fields are marked as PSI/PII.
blocks.text: The selected fields are marked as PSI/PII.

blocks.raw: ## Classifying behavioural event attributes as PSI
blocks.text: Classifying behavioural event attributes as PSI

blocks.raw: You can mark behavioural event attributes as PSI when [creating or editing a behavioural event](https://docs.capillarytech.com/docs/setup-test-behavioral-events).
blocks.text: You can mark behavioural event attributes as PSI when creating or editing a behavioural event.

blocks.raw: When you add an attribute to an event, select the PSI option to mark it as sensitive.
blocks.text: When you add an attribute to an event, select the PSI option to mark it as sensitive.
